analysis.title: Chile Copper: Labour Negotiations Add Another Supply Risk Into 2027
key_insights: Cochilco now expects Chilean copper production to fall 8.4% YoY to 4.94Mt in 2026. A year ago it forecast +3.7% (+200kt) to 5.61Mt. That is a ~670kt downgrade and a ~12ppt swing in expected growth.

Chilean output excluding Escondida and the QB ramp-up has fallen 20% since 2020, and output is at its lowest level in more than 20 years, about 650kt below pre-2020 levels. Weather, safety incidents, ageing assets and underinvestment (partly from policy uncertainty) have contributed.
Copper has risen 50% in three years, yet Western miners still struggle to deliver planned volumes.
Mines representing GSe 3.45Mt, or 60-65% of Chilean copper supply, enter labour contract negotiations through end-2027. The unions involved cover 40-45% (~18k workers) of their direct workforce.

BHP has the greatest exposure through Escondida and Spence (GSe ~75% of its copper production). Other GSe exposure shares: RIO ~35% (Escondida), LUN ~40% (Caserones), ANTO ~55% (Los Pelambres) and ~30% (Centinela).
GLEN (Lomas Bayas) and AAL (El Soldado) have more limited exposure, and neither operation has a history of industrial action.

Escondida's Sindicato No.1 is Chile's largest single mining union and held the longest strike in Chilean history (44 days in 2017). Its contract expires Aug-27. Escondida and Caserones have a history of industrial action.
Widespread industrial action is not GS's base case, but the scale of the 2027 negotiation calendar is notable while Chilean production is already under pressure.

High copper prices raise the stakes. Strong margins may support higher union expectations, safety focus has increased after several fatalities, and the government expects mining underperformance to cut Chilean GDP by 1-1.5%.
Higher copper prices have not historically meant more strikes. Strike disruption has fallen materially since the 2017 labour reform, and disputes are increasingly settled through negotiation.

Recent settlements point to elevated compensation expectations. Mantoverde had a 35-day strike and Centinela a 10-day strike before settling. A strike was averted at Escondida after supervisors (Sindicato No.2) agreed to a reported ~US$27k bonus, ~25% higher in real terms than the 2023 settlement.
Post-mediation settlements have generally delivered higher wage increases in GS's disclosed sample, though reaching mediation means talks are closer to potential industrial action.
Escondida output has fallen below its historical range, and El Teniente output is ~40% below its historical median ahead of 2027 negotiations covering ~80% of its direct workforce.
Chilean copper output is down ~8.5% YTD, tracking at more than 20-year lows.

market_movers.rationale: Greatest exposure to 2027 Chilean labour negotiations through Escondida and Spence (GSe ~75% of copper production). Spence supervisors' contract expires Nov-26 and Escondida's largest union Aug-27.
Exposed through its Escondida stake (~35% of copper production) to the Aug-27 negotiation with Chile's largest mining union.
Lundin Mining (LUN) has ~40% of copper production at Caserones, which has a history of industrial action and three contract expiries in Apr-27 and Jul-27.
Antofagasta (ANTO) has ~55% of copper production at Los Pelambres and ~30% at Centinela. Centinela's recent 10-day strike is a precedent, though Los Pelambres' union is smaller.

sector_views.rationale: GS flags labour negotiations as a further supply risk into 2027 for Chilean copper but says widespread industrial action is not its base case.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Cochilco's forecast is ~670kt below its forecast of a year ago (5.61Mt, +3.7%), a supply shortfall in the largest copper producing country.

macro_indicators.indicator: Chilean GDP impact of mining underperformance (government expectation)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Government pressure to recover lost production raises the cost of disruption for miners and the economy.
Monthly output is tracking at more than 20-year lows.

risk_factors: Industrial action across Chilean copper mines through 2027, with unions covering 40-45% of the direct workforce at mines making up 60-65% of supply.
Escondida Sindicato No.1 contract expiry in Aug-27, given its 44-day strike in 2017.
Higher union expectations from strong copper margins and recent settlement bonuses.
Safety incidents after several fatalities at larger, mature mines.
Weather, ageing assets and underinvestment adding to operational disruption.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 lists Chilean mining union contract expirations from Nov-26 to Dec-27, covering 3.45Mt of 2027 production and 42% of the workforce.
Exhibit 9 shows the highest reported settlement bonus at Escondida in 2024 at CLP36mn (US$38k).
geopolitical: Chilean policy uncertainty has partly contributed to underinvestment in the copper industry.
Chilean government expects mining underperformance to reduce GDP by 1-1.5%, adding pressure to recover lost production.

tension_points.bull_case: Strike disruption has fallen materially since the 2017 labour reform, and disputes are increasingly resolved through negotiated settlements. Higher copper prices have not historically meant more strikes.
tension_points.bear_case: 60-65% of Chilean supply enters negotiations through end-2027. Recent settlements show elevated compensation expectations, and high copper prices raise the stakes. Escondida's largest union has a history of striking.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Escondida Workers' Union No. 1 failing to settle at its Aug-27 contract expiry, or more strikes like the 35-day Mantoverde and 10-day Centinela stoppages.

theme_stances.key_argument: Labour negotiations covering most Chilean copper supply add another supply risk into 2027, though widespread industrial action is not the base case.
